item.title: Effect of pore diameter and orientation on ductile fracture of laser powder bed fusion stainless steel 316L
item.description: 库内相似论文：High strain rate effect on tensile ductility and fracture of AM fabricated inconel 718 with voided microstructures（相似度 0.827） 引用重点论文：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 引用重点论文：Micromechanically-motivated phenomenological Hosford–Coulomb model for predicting ductile fracture initiation at low stress triaxialities [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijsolstr.2015.02.024] 引用重点论文：A new model of metal plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] 与《Orientation and stress state dependent plasticity and damage initiation behavior of stainless steel 304L manufactured by laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing》共享 7 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.226 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1430882450, https://openalex.org/W2032768430, https://openalex.org/W2762367303, https://openalex.org/W2790889497, item.title: Stress state dependent deformation and fracture mechanism transition of Ti80 alloy

plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] 与《Lode dependent plasticity coupled with nonlinear damage accumulation for ductile fracture of item.title: Cyclic deformation and fatigue damage evolution of additively manufactured porous titanium alloys at 550°C
item.description: 库内相似论文：Multiaxial and non-proportional loading responses, anisotropy and modeling of ti–6Al–4V titanium alloy over wide ranges of strain rates and temperatures（相似度 0.804） 增材 TC4 缺陷与力学响应: 可作为缺陷形貌与成形方向如何改变塑性流动和断裂行为的机制线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对是否给出应力应变或断裂数据（而非只有组织照片）、制备参数与热处理状态、是否与你的试样同一工艺窗口 仅题名片段: Cyclic deformation and fatigue damage evolution … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 损伤演化与孔洞机制: 可作为损伤累积形式与孔洞机制建模的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对损伤变量定义、是否与塑性耦合、单元尺寸依赖是否处理 仅题名片段: Cyclic deformation and fatigue damage evolution … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: item.title: A coupled mechanics model for perforation of finite metal plates by deformable flat-nosed projectiles: Projectile upsetting, shear plugging and global plate deformation
item.description: 库内相似论文：Deformation and perforation of thin metal plate under normal penetration of elliptical cross-section projectiles（相似度 0.854） 与《Plasticity, ductile fracture and ballistic impact item.title: Tensile and compressive properties of a nickel-based single-crystal superalloy by the combined influences of high temperatures and high strain rates

Separating the soaking and deformation temperatures provides a means of tailoring the elevated-temperature response of Ti-6Al-4V sheet before rapid forming. Direct-heating (DH) and step-quenching (SQ) tensile responses were compared at subtransus temperatures and nominal strain rates of 0.1, 1 and 5 s-1. SQ from 950 °C reduced the flow stress relative to DH at the same deformation temperature, but its effect on hardening and softening was strongly rate dependent. The 950→800 °C route exhibited prolonged hardening at 0.1 s-1 while retaining substantial softening at 5 s-1. A 900→850 °C route provided a more balanced response, combining a lower flow stress than DH850 °C with reduced softening and positive apparent rate dependence. Post-test microscopy showed route- and rate-dependent α morphologies and image-derived α fractions consistent with the different thermal exposures and deformation times. A thermal-history-dependent constitutive formulation based on the Gavrus mixture framework was calibrated using the DH and 950 °C-based SQ datasets and subsequently assessed against the 900→850 °C route, capturing the principal stress, strain and rate trends over the calibrated strain range. A previously demonstrated cup with 1.8 draw ratio formed using the 900→850 °C route was further assessed at component level. The maximum measured thickness reduction was 12.7% near the punch corner. The simulation reproduced the overall thickness-profile trend and predicted considerable spatial variations in equivalent plastic strain and temperature during the 0.38 s draw. Post-form microscopy showed corresponding spatial changes in primary α morphology. The results identify the SQ900→850 °C route as a practical compromise within the tested matrix and demonstrate the importance of thermal history alongside instantaneous forming temperature and strain rate. In the fabrication of biomedical sheet components from next-generation Zn-Ag-Cu-based alloys, establishing the relationship between the material's directional plastic behavior and the limits of multiaxial forming is of critical importance. This study presents an integrated analytical-numerical approach developed to convert the mechanical properties of solid alloys into direction-dependent sheet properties and forming limit diagrams. A distinctive feature of this methodology is the theoretical estimation of plastic anisotropy coefficients based on a proposed analytical approximation that incorporates alloy composition and crystal lattice geometry. These estimated coefficients were incorporated into a finite element model via directional yield stresses. For three independent datasets, elastic properties were determined using the Voigt-Reuss-Hill approach, hardening behavior was modeled with the Hollomon equation, and the anisotropic yield surface was approximated using the Hill48 criterion. The resulting synthetic sheet material cards were utilized in virtual Nakajima tests involving seven specimen geometries, where the onset of local necking was determined from time-dependent changes in strain histories at critical points. While the minimum predicted major limit strains ranged from 0.038 to 0.111 across the datasets in paths near plane strain, the major limit strain in the uniaxial loading region reached 0.371. In contrast, the limits in the biaxial tensile region converged within the range of 0.328–0.345. This analysis demonstrates that formability differences among material models become particularly evident in deformation paths close to uniaxial and in-plane strain. These findings represent preliminary computational predictions, and further experimental microstructural testing is required to verify actual sheet formability. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Ballistic+performance+of+gradient+nanostructured+magnesium+alloys+against+spherical+projec&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.11.112%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22impact_validation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Magnesium alloys hold substantial potential for lightweight armor applications due to their low density and high specific strength. However, their low absolute strength has restricted their large–scale engineering applications. To address this problem, explosive hardening (EH) was employed to fabricate a gradient nanostructure (GNS) with a depth of 14 mm in AZ31 magnesium alloy (AZ31 Mg alloy), thereby enhancing its mechanical properties and ballistic performance. Experimental and numerical simulation methods were integrated to investigate the microstructure, mechanical properties, and ballistic performance of the GNS AZ31 Mg alloy. Mechanical tests reveal significant improvements in GNS AZ31 compared to untreated specimens: a 63% increase in microhardness, a 107% enhancement in tensile yield strength, and a 59% rise in dynamic compressive yield strength. Ballistic tests yield an observed 6.3% rise in fitted ballistic limit (372 m/s for GNS AZ31 versus 350 m/s for the untreated alloy). Both targets display petal–shaped cracking under low–velocity perforation and plugging failure at high impact velocities. The untreated AZ31 Mg alloy suffers plugging failure at 368 m/s, whereas GNS AZ31 still shows prominent petal–shaped cracking at 384 m/s, indicating delayed shear deformation during perforation. Finite element (FE) simulations confirm a multi-stage energy-dissipation mechanism in GNS AZ31. Gradient-matched layer properties allow the high-strength surface to withstand initial projectile impact and lower-strength inner layers to dissipate residual energy. This hierarchical gradient design improves energy-absorption capacity, suggesting EH-induced GNS is a promising route toward advanced lightweight armor materials. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+unified+strain+energy+decomposition+framework+for+phase-field+fracture+modelling&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijmecsci.2026.112231%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In the phase-field modelling framework, strain energy is commonly decomposed into positive and negative components to capture the tension–compression asymmetry of materials. Nevertheless, most existing decomposition strategies are valid only for specific stress-state cases, limiting their applicability in simulating fracture propagation in real-world structures that often experience complex and varying stress conditions. To overcome this limitation, a unified strain energy decomposition framework applicable to arbitrary stress states is proposed. Within this framework, the elastic strain energy is divided into three non-negative components, namely tensile, shear and compressive strain energy. A local coordinate system is determined by maximising the F -function energy dissipation, which drives the damage evolution. Depending on the ratio of shear to tensile fracture toughness and the value of Poisson’s ratio, the proposed unified framework can degenerate into existing decomposition schemes such as the spectral, volumetric–deviatoric (V–D), or crack-direction-based decomposition methods under specific stress states. The unified phase-field model, implemented in ABAQUS platform through the VUEL and VUMAT subroutines, was verified via a single-element benchmark and subsequently validated through a series of numerical examples under tensile, compressive, and shear stress states. Those results illustrated that the proposed energy decomposition framework consistently reproduces fracture evolution across arbitrary stress states, showing superior generality, robustness, and accuracy compared with currently existing decomposition approaches. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+constitutive+framework+for+fracture+mode+diagram+of+hydrogen-degraded+steels%3A+coupled+vo&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.ijhydene.2026.158526%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22damage_evolution%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Hydrogen-charged steels often show quasi-cleavage (QC) near the surface and ductile dimples in the bulk. In the proposed model, void nucleation, growth, distortion, coalescence and QC compete at each material point under a single damage criterion. The QC rate law describes hydrogen-enhanced decohesion mediated by localised plasticity (HELP-mediated HEDE), driven by the Mori–Tanaka-recovered matrix stress and gated by hydrogen availability, and only QC and distortion damage are regularised non-locally. Coupled with hydrogen transport, the model is applied to X70-type smooth bars at various hydrogen concentrations and Péclet numbers ( Pe ). QC failure requires a threshold concentration, initiates at the surface and penetrates deeper as Pe decreases. With increasing hydrogen, the reduction of area at first failure falls from 84–85% to 25–26% almost independently of Pe , whereas the strain to crack 10% of the section decreases with Pe . Equal- Pe analyses coincide, and QC competes with ductile failure only through matrix-stress amplification. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Unified+constitutive+model+of+body-centered+cubic+metals+informed+by+discrete+dislocation+&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.48550%2Farxiv.2611.17617%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design. Abstract This study investigates the fatigue behavior, tensile properties, and microstructural characteristics of Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) specimens produced by electron beam melting (EBM). Ti-6Al-4V is widely used in aerospace, rocketry, marine, and biomedical applications owing to its high specific strength, thermal stability, and corrosion resistance. The influence of key EBM process parameters on surface quality was established across 25 parameter combinations, and as-printed specimen density was determined by hydrostatic weighing. Microstructural homogeneity was assessed through Vickers hardness mapping and SEM analysis. High-cycle fatigue tests were conducted at a stress ratio of Rₛ = 0.1, and S-N curves were constructed and compared against reference data for conventionally produced Ti-6Al-4V. While the tensile strength of as-printed material (Rₘ = 959…974 MPa, δ = 6.5…8.5%) met or exceeded the requirements for annealed Grade 5 product forms, fatigue life was found to be significantly lower under the tested process conditions — fatigue limit Δσ c,50% = 201 MPa at 2∙10⁶ cycles compared to 520 MPa for the reference material. Fractographic analysis by scanning electron microscopy identified inter-layer lack-of-fusion defects and clusters of unmelted powder particles as primary fatigue crack initiation sites, directly attributable to insufficient volumetric energy density at 100 µm layer thickness. The results demonstrate that satisfactory static strength is an insufficient qualification criterion for fatigue-critical EBM aerospace components, and that strict process parameter control is essential. Abstract Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite ( γ N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired γ N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting γ N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF. The dynamic coupling between plastic deformation and precipitation has important implications for warm forming of high strength aluminium alloys, which is a promising process for weight saving of complex shaped structural parts. In this study, Small Angle X-ray Scattering in situ tensile tests have been performed on underaged Al-Zn-Mg-Cu samples over a wide parameter space including initial state, temperature and strain rate, to understand the influence of supersaturation and deformation conditions on dynamic precipitation. We observe that deformation accelerates the precipitation kinetics in these underaged alloys, due to the production of excess vacancies during plastic deformation. Depending on the combination of temperature and supersaturation, this acceleration results in an acceleration of growth or a precipitate dissolution. In case of accelerated growth, an acceleration factor is proposed to quantify the acceleration due to deformation. Higher strain rates result in faster kinetics, and the effect of deformation is stronger in less supersaturated systems. Temperature has a more complex influence, as it affects both the production and annihilation rate of excess vacancies. We discuss the obtained data in relation to the classical model of vacancy production which does not fully describe the complex phenomena observed, particularly the rapid annihilation of vacancies following deformation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Thermo-mechanical+mechanisms+in+induction-assisted+hard+turning+of+SKD61+steel+revealed+by&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1038%2Fs41598-026-78092-2%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22stress_state%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 This study presents a mechanism-centered thermo-mechanical reanalysis of induction-assisted hard turning of hardened SKD61 steel with high-speed steel tools using a previously published, center-weighted 27-run campaign as the experimental benchmark. No new authenticated cutting simulations were performed; the numerical contribution comprises reanalysis of archived FEM outputs, Johnson–Cook constitutive-sensitivity calculations, and verification-oriented post-processing. At the condition-matched 475 °C reference, the archived FEM cutting force differed from the experimental mean by 1.43%. Sensitivity screening identified the initial yield parameter \(A\) and thermal-softening exponent \(m\) as the dominant local constitutive influences, with the effect of \(m\) increasing with temperature. From 350 to 600 °C, the archived flank-contact-pressure indicator decreased from 920 to 680 MPa, whereas predicted average tool-zone temperature increased from 430 to 525 °C. Under matched cutting parameters, \({R}_{a}\) , \({R}_{q}\) , and \({R}_{z}\) decreased by about 29%, while terminal \(V{B}_{\text{m}\text{a}\text{x}}\) remained broadly overlapping and non-monotonic across the three temperatures. The limited wear subset supports endpoint comparison only, not wear-rate or tool-life inference. The 475 °C condition is therefore interpreted as an intermediate thermo-mechanical state, not a renewed optimum. Conclusions are limited by the archived 2D plane-strain formulation and the absence of independent tool-temperature validation. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Development+and+experimental+validation+of+element+node-based+overstressed+fraction+method&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.rineng.2026.114214%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Additive manufacturing and additive-specific design, such as generative design, are mutually reinforcing solutions. The result obtained from finite element validation of parts resulting from such a design, which shows the surface or volumetric stress distribution in complex parts where many surfaces meet, is difficult to objectively evaluate, based on the given threshold and subjectively make a decision on the suitability of the part based on the appearance of parts above it. In this research, we address this challenge by selective laser melting of Ti6Al4V alloys in parts subjected to torsional loading. A theoretical method was developed to determine and examine the change in the ratio of finite elements above the threshold. The characteristic point was determined, based on which the torque required for fracture failure can be predicted. After numerical validation of the theoretical method, it was further validated on real 3D-printed parts using torque measurements. Based on the results, the developed method can more accurately predict the load at which the component will fail before costly printing. This allows objective verification of the design limits or, if these are unavailable, determination of the failure limit. Published: 2026-11-01T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Results in Engineering 研究类型: TC4核心研究

The ductile deformation of an AA1050 aluminium polycrystal is investigated using in-situ multimodal X-ray imaging that combines phase-contrast tomography (PCT), diffraction contrast tomography (DCT), and scanning 3D X-ray diffraction (S-3DXRD). A 3D experimental grain map of the undeformed sample with grain shapes and orientations obtained from DCT is used as input for a crystal-plasticity finite-element (CP-FE) model. Void nucleation and growth across the entire necking region of the sample are visualised as a function of plastic strain using PCT. S-3DXRD measurements - yielding spatially resolved intragranular orientation and stress fields - are performed on the layer where the first deformation-induced void appears at an engineering stress near the ultimate tensile strength and an engineering strain of 0.4. The same layer is remapped at a strain of 1.0 - well into the necking regime but far from fracture, where two additional voids have formed. At the strain of 0.4 at the nucleation site of one of these, an extended region of extreme stress triaxiality was observed. After nucleation and growth, the triaxiality in this region had decreased at the strain of 1.0. The triaxiality remained at a high level in the grains containing all three voids. The experimentally measured spatial stress distributions show good agreement with CP-FE predictions. The void growth prediction by the Rice-Tracey equation, using the local CP-FE stress triaxialities, successfully reproduces the shape of void-growth curves for two voids studied. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Fracture+anisotropy+in+additively+manufactured+SS+316L%3A+A+phase-field+approach&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1177%2F10567895261484693%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Additively manufactured (AM) metallic components often exhibit pronounced anisotropy due to deposition-induced microstructural features, which strongly influence their deformation and fracture behavior. In this work, a coupled anisotropic phase-field fracture framework incorporating rate-independent elastoplasticity is developed to model fracture in directed energy deposited AISI 316L stainless steel, with explicit sensitivity to deposition direction. The formulation combines isotropic linear elasticity with stress-based spectral decomposition to ensure tension–compression asymmetry. Fracture anisotropy is introduced through a structural tensor embedded in the crack surface density function, while plastic deformation is described using classical J 2 plasticity with isotropic hardening. The model preserves the variational structure of the phase-field approach, with plasticity influencing fracture indirectly through the evolution of elastic strains and a crack-driving history variable. An extensive experimental campaign, including quasi-static tensile testing of specimens extracted along multiple build orientations, digital image correlation, and microstructural and fractographic analyses, is conducted to characterize anisotropic mechanical response and failure mechanisms. Numerical simulations successfully reproduce the experimentally observed orientation-dependent stress–strain behavior, crack paths, and fracture modes, demonstrating the capability of the proposed framework to capture the interplay between plasticity, anisotropy, and fracture in AM metals. The results highlight the critical role of deposition direction in governing fracture resistance and provide a robust predictive tool for failure analysis of AM structures. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Effect+of+low-power+remelting+process+on+the+formed+specimen+of+TC4+titanium+alloy+by+sele&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1108%2Frpj-10-2025-0512%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Purpose This study aims to investigate the SLM remelting process and improved the overall performance of the formed samples greatly. It provides a strategy for effectively manufacturing high melting point materials such as TC4 on machines with limited laser power. By designing the experiment of the low-power remelting process (LPRP), the difference between direct high power forming quality and low power forming quality is explored. Which provides new considerations for SLM low-power forming TC4 specimens. Design/methodology/approach This experiment is based on energy density. In the experimental parameters, to ensure the sum of the remelting process energy density and the volume process forming energy density was consistent. Using different volume laser powers and remelting laser powers to form samples. Findings The authors found that using LPRP can form specimens with good surface quality and density, and the metallographic structure is beneficial to the mechanical properties. This method can use low-power equipment to form high melting point materials, reduce excessive energy gradients, produce multiple α' phases, and improve the overall performance of the specimen. Originality/value The LPRP has the following advantages: 1) Reduces the excessive energy gradient to produce multiple α' phases; 2) Provides a strategy for effectively manufacturing high melting point materials such as TC4 on machines with limited laser power. item.category: 跨圈方法发现（非近期新作）

item.category: International Journal of Solids and Structures
跨圈方法发现（非近期新作）
item.description: 跨圈方法发现（非近期新作） 库内相似论文：Modelling metal plasticity and damage with constitutive artificial neural networks（相似度 0.836） 与《Inverse identification of the post-necking work hardening behaviour of thick HSS through full-field strain measurements during diffuse necking》共享 2 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.066 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W200825189, https://openalex.org/W2033327909 其他金属的同链研究: 研究链一致时与钛合金同等参考价值；建模思路、标定流程与验证方案可直接借鉴（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对材料体系差异与微观机制是否可比；参数量级不可直接套用，需在 TC4 上重新标定 仅题名片段: Physics-informed machine learning for constitutive modeling … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知
